title: Military Fellowship Program: Supply Chain Program Manager
jd_text: SNC's Military Fellowship Program partners with programs such as SkillBridge and Hiring Our Heroes to provide fellowship opportunities to service members transitioning to the civilian workforce. These fellowships include up to six months of on-the-job industry training for eligible service members. During this time, participants gain valuable work experience in the civilian sector and build professional networks as they prepare for their transition to full-time civilian work. NOTE: You must be currently serving on active duty to be eligible for this fellowship program. This program is not for veterans who have already separated from the military. Staffed out of Supply Chain and assigned to a program or proposal, Supply Chain Program Managers (SCPMs) are the primary experts for both Supply Chain Program Management and Technical responsibility of a Supplier’s SOW. As a SCPM, you may oversee daily operations for multiple lower-level SCPMs and/or Supply Chain Project Coordinators (SCPCs). You will be accountable for the overall supply chain performance of the business unit or large, complex programs’ including cost, technical, schedule planning, and execution. You will collaborate with assigned Subcontract Leads, Purchasing Agents, Program Office staff, Engineering teams, Operations personnel, and Business Management to develop strategies that meet program missions. This includes ensuring timely completion of all technical requirements documentation as well as maintaining adequate labor/non-labor budgets. The role involves consolidating supply chain risks at the program level while mitigating them effectively. You will also act as a key voice in developing supplier requirements during proposals. This role may require the following responsibilities: Leadership and Team Supervision • Supervise a team of SCPCs and SCPM 1, providing daily oversight and guidance on SNC's tools, procedures, and processes. • Participate in and occasionally lead programmatic and technical meetings with subcontractors and suppliers. • Attend Program Reviews with subcontractors to provide updates, communicate needs and status, and request program-driven changes Strategic Supply Chain Management and Planning • Develop the Program-level Supply Chain Management Plan, outlining supply chain strategies, reporting, and communication plan. • Develop a cohesive strategy for forming effective teaming within our supply chain network which encompasses a robust framework that ensures seamless integration. • Develop comprehensive negotiation strategies to facilitate the formalization of strategic agreements with key suppliers. • Create tailored sourcing strategies that address each category's unique requirements and actively engage cross-functional teams in collaborative planning sessions. • Evaluate the performance and capabilities of current suppliers and the supply chain, forecast future needs, and develop negotiation strategies that promote sustained collaboration. • May be responsible to lead make / buy assessments from supply chain perspective. • May be assigned as the subcontract Program Manager for a large or complex subcontract, executing the role of Program Manager. • If assigned to a platform, product line, Business Unit (BU) or product support team, collaborate and communicate potential long-term investment strategies to reduce lead-time and cost. • Identify and coordinate the need for alternate or additional sources to enhance competition and leverage. Act as the supply chain architect and liaison for the proposal or program, ensuring a competitive, capable, and compliant supply base • Lead business requirements, technical evaluations, risk assessments, and Basis of Estimate (BOE) strategies in support of proposals and new pursuits. • Provide supply chain strategy and status to internal and external customers • Support SNC's Design for Excellence (Dfx) initiatives by leading the Design for Supply Chain (DFSC) efforts, including implementing Design to Product Target Cost (DPTC) methodologies for development programs. • Support department goals, objectives and supply chain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), such as on-time delivery, negotiations, and purchase requisition processing time Supply Chain Communication and Coordination • Act as the liaison between the Supply Chain management team and the program to ensure alignment of prime requirements (i.e., CDRLs to SDRLs) and timely resolution of problems. • Initiate the Purchase Requisition (PR) to Purchase Order (PO) process by developing the Material and Service Request (MSR) or Advanced Purchase Requisition (APL). • Create and update Supply Chain Program Review Charts, dashboards, highlighting the current cost, technical, and schedule performance of each program. • Coordinate between supply chain teams (procurement, subcontract management, and the program) to ensure timely schedules and milestone delivery. • Communicate supply chain status, identify/manage risk and opportunity. • Champion and present status of recovery plans to all stakeholders at the program level or to senior supply chain leadership. Program Management and Control Account • Manage the cost, technical, and schedule aspects of supply chain for a given proposal or program as the Program Management representative. • Track progress against the Supply Chain schedule, identifying and addressing any deviations. • Lead the development of Supplier/Subcontractor Statements of Work (SSOW), Supplier Data Requirement Lists (SDRLs), and other requirements flow downs. • Identify potential risks within program specific supply chain (subcontractors and procured parts) and present mitigation plans to address risk. • May be delegated Control Account Manager (CAM) responsibilities by the Program Manager, requiring SCPM to obtain SNC’s CAM Certification. • Use Earned Value Management (EVM) techniques to assess project performance • Monitor actual costs against budgeted costs and report variances. • Calculate, track and report out on key EVM metrics, such as Cost Performance Index (CPI) and Schedule Performance Index (SPI), to all stakeholders. • Prepare regular status reports on cost, schedule, and performance metrics. Maintain comprehensive documentation related to all aspects of the control account. • Analyze causes behind significant variances from planned values in terms both time/costs recommending corrective actions where necessary. Additional SCPM proposal/pursuit responsibilities: As an SCPM supporting pursuits and proposal activities, you will ensure SNC is well-positioned with an achievable solution and a competitive, compliant, and capable supply base to win new business. Specific tasks may include: • Collaborate with supply chain team to; o Identify potential supply sources to mitigate risks, identify opportunities and meet program objectives. o Develop source selection strategies, criteria, and planning, including participation in Make/Buy assessments at the program level. • Create and document labor and non-labor Basis of Estimates (BOE). • Develop program/technical requirements documents. • Support technical evaluation of proposals for content and quality. • Lead or support the development of source selection plans, mitigating risks by qualifying multiple sources, and practice split awards when possible. Present business cases to Program Management and Supply Chain Leadership. • Provide subcontractor and critical procurement-related input into customer proposals. • Ensure subcontractors' milestone payment plans align with program expectations, budget, and schedules. • Develop a preliminary Supply Chain Management Plan that includes resources for successful new program start-up. title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Vision AI
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Most TPM roles focus on tracking timelines, coordinating milestones, and driving execution against an established plan. This role is different. You’ll own the operational backbone of a vision AI data program, ensuring ideas move seamlessly from hypothesis to data capture to validation to a governed dataset to a commercial product. You’ll sit at the center of a complex ecosystem spanning a lean founding engineering team, capture hardware and annotation vendors, frontier AI and robotics companies, academic partners, and internal Legal, Site Operations, and Finance teams. Your mandate is to create operational continuity across these interfaces, remove friction, accelerate decisions, and maintain a disciplined path from experimentation to validated, production ready outcomes. Stord Labs is an innovation center designed to evaluate emerging logistics technologies and help redefine the future of fulfillment. Within a live micro fulfillment environment, you’ll orchestrate the full lifecycle of technical experiments, ensuring promising concepts are rigorously tested, clearly validated, and efficiently transitioned into production when they demonstrate measurable business value. This role is built for a systems oriented program leader who has operated in computer vision, ML, AI, robotics, or data intensive environments and can translate fluently between research, engineering, and warehouse operations without sacrificing speed or precision. You’ll be equally comfortable working with engineers and researchers, coordinating external partners, navigating operational constraints, and communicating outcomes to executive stakeholders. The goal isn’t simply to manage the program. It’s to build the operating system that allows a new vision AI capability to move from idea to validated data product at scale. What You'll Do: Own the evaluation lifecycle: Govern the end to end pipeline of experiments, ensuring every initiative starts with a clear hypothesis, measurable success criteria, and structured evaluation framework. Drive disciplined decisions to kill, iterate, or scale based on evidence. Run hardware and vendor evaluations: Lead structured, evidence based evaluations across capture devices, depth sensors, gloves, edge compute, and data and annotation vendors. Own RFPs, scorecards, evaluation frameworks, and vendor selection. Orchestrate the cross functional ecosystem: Serve as the primary integration point between the engineering pod and Legal, Site Operations, Finance, and warehouse operations. Coordinate requirements around consent, associate participation, scheduling, floor logistics, cost modeling, and operational readiness. Manage the data pipeline program: Drive the path from pilot capture through annotation, validation, and secure buyer delivery. Own annotation throughput and QA cadence while establishing and tracking data quality, capture yield, and delivery metrics. Manage partners and buyers: Coordinate technical and operational engagement with frontier AI and robotics companies and academic partners such as Georgia Tech. Translate customer requirements into clear program priorities and ensure datasets meet the standards required for validation and delivery. Keep governance and risk on track: Ensure consent, privacy, and data rights requirements are addressed with Legal before and throughout capture activities. Identify and retire program risks while keeping executive sponsors informed of progress, tradeoffs, and decisions. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical discipline. 8+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Management, or complex cross functional delivery roles. Demonstrated experience running computer vision, ML, or data pipeline programs end to end, including data collection, annotation, model training pipelines, or data platform delivery. Proven experience managing both hardware and data or annotation vendors, including RFPs, structured evaluations, scorecards, and strategic partnerships. Comfortable operating in deeply technical CV, ML, and data environments and translating between research, engineering, and operations without losing precision. Strong execution discipline and experience operating in agile, sprint based, or similar environments. Demonstrated judgment in making and driving kill, iterate, or scale decisions based on data and outcomes. High ownership and comfort operating in ambiguous, 0 to 1 environments. Bonus Points: Experience in innovation labs, R&D environments, or advanced automation programs. Familiarity with egocentric or robotics datasets, annotation platforms such as Scale, MLOps, or delivering datasets to external customers. Experience with data governance, privacy, or consent programs, including BIPA, GDPR, or CCPA requirements. Familiarity with warehouse data ecosystems and architectures, including WMS, OMS, WES, and WCS. Exposure to digital twin or simulation initiatives. Domain knowledge in warehouse automation, robotics integration, or fulfillment operations. Experience working with frontier AI companies, robotics companies, academic research institutions, or other emerging technology partners.

With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Role Overview The Program Manager, Compliance is a strategic driver of Stord’s operational strength and commercial growth. This role is responsible for scaling enterprise compliance programs across OSHA, EPA, GMP, and adjacent regulatory regimes -- building the infrastructure that enables Stord to operate with confidence, win in the market, and deliver on the compliance commitments that today’s leading brands require from a fulfillment partner. A mature, well-run compliance program is not just a risk management function at Stord; it is a competitive differentiator that unlocks customer revenue, supports network expansion, and protects the business at scale. Reporting to the Director of Health, Safety & Security, this is an enterprise-level, network-wide role that operates at the intersection of compliance, operations, and growth. The Program Manager partners closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Finance to ensure compliance capabilities are a strength Stord leads with -- enabling the business to pursue regulated customer segments, scale into new markets, and demonstrate the program maturity that top-tier brands demand. The work product of this role is what the entire organization is built around: scalable written programs, audit frameworks, certification standards, reporting infrastructure, and regulatory intelligence systems that grow stronger as Stord grows. What This Role Owns This role owns the enterprise compliance program architecture -- the standards, written programs, audit frameworks, and governance mechanisms that define what ‘compliant’ looks like at every Stord facility. The work product of this role is what the rest of the organization is held accountable to. Specifically: Enterprise compliance program design, construction, and ownership across OSHA, EPA, GMP, GDP, DOT, and applicable state and local regulatory frameworks -- building programs from the ground up where gaps exist and elevating inconsistent standards to enterprise-grade. Regulatory intelligence: continuously monitoring rulemaking, agency guidance, and enforcement trends; converting regulatory change into updated enterprise programs before gaps become violations. Enterprise audit and inspection framework: designing the internal audit program architecture, defining scope and methodology, and building the tools and cadences that keep the network inspection-ready -- not conducting site audits, but building the system that governs them. Enterprise compliance documentation infrastructure: designing and owning the system of record for all written programs, SOPs, training requirements, certifications, and regulatory correspondence -- the single source of truth for compliance across the network. Customer and industry certification programs: GMP, GDP, CTPAT, TAPA, and other regulated operating standards required by Stord’s customer base. Regulatory agency relationships: serving as the primary compliance point of contact for OSHA, EPA, and other agencies at the program level. Enterprise compliance reporting, data, and dashboards: building the metrics infrastructure that gives the Head of HSS, senior leadership, and the broader business real-time visibility into compliance performance, risk posture, and program health across the network. Enterprise compliance training architecture: defining what training is required, for whom, at what frequency, and in what format -- building the content and governance framework that regional and site teams deliver against. Key Responsibilities OSHA Compliance Program Management Build and own Stord’s enterprise OSHA compliance program -- designing the written program architecture, establishing network-wide standards, and creating the governance mechanisms that ensure consistent compliance across every facility regardless of size, volume, or operational complexity. Maintain and update OSHA-required written programs: Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout, Respiratory Protection, Emergency Action Plans, Powered Industrial Truck programs, and others as applicable. Oversee OSHA recordkeeping standards across the network -- establishing recordkeeping protocols, auditing site-level logs for accuracy, and managing 300A summary posting requirements. Serve as the primary internal resource for OSHA compliance questions, inspection preparation, and citation response -- coordinating with Legal and the Head of HSS on formal agency interactions. Track OSHA rulemaking, enforcement priorities, and National Emphasis Programs relevant to warehouse and fulfillment operations; update programs proactively. Develop and maintain OSHA compliance self-assessment tools for use by Regional Managers and Site Managers. EPA and Environmental Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise EPA compliance program -- designing the framework that covers applicable Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, EPCRA, and Tier II reporting obligations across the network and scales as the facility footprint grows. Maintain environmental compliance calendars for all sites, ensuring permit renewals, required inspections, and mandatory reporting deadlines are met without exception. Manage Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans and storm water pollution prevention programs where applicable. Coordinate with Facilities and Operations on environmental requirements triggered by site construction, expansion, or changes in chemical inventory. Serve as the point of escalation for environmental incidents, regulatory notifications, and corrective actions related to EPA-regulated activities. Monitor EPA regulatory changes and enforcement activity relevant to Stord’s operations; assess impact and update compliance programs accordingly. GMP, GDP, and Regulated Operating Standards Build and own Stord’s enterprise GMP and GDP compliance programs -- designing the standards, SOPs, and qualification frameworks that enable Stord to onboard and serve regulated customers at scale across health, wellness, supplement, and pharmaceutical-adjacent accounts. Develop and maintain GMP/GDP-aligned SOPs, documentation standards, and control requirements applicable to regulated fulfillment operations. Lead readiness activities for GMP and GDP customer audits and third-party certifications -- managing pre-audit assessments, coordinating site preparation, and tracking corrective action plans post-audit. Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to assess GMP/GDP requirements for new customer onboarding and ensure facilities are qualified before regulated product is received. Maintain working knowledge of FDA guidance, NSF, and other applicable standards that intersect with Stord’s customer base and product handling requirements. Build and maintain a GMP/GDP compliance library: training materials, audit checklists, SOP templates, and certification documentation for use across the network. Hazmat and Chemical Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise Hazardous Materials compliance program -- designing the program for our fulfillment locations, OSHA Hazard Communication, EPA chemical reporting, and state-specific requirements across the full facility network. Maintain the enterprise Hazmat program: classification standards, handling and storage requirements, labeling, SDS management systems, and spill response frameworks. Establish and maintain Hazmat acceptance criteria and screening processes to ensure sites are equipped to handle regulated materials received from customers. Coordinate Hazmat compliance requirements with Transportation, Operations, and Facilities during new site launches, customer onboarding, and facility modifications. Manage DOT compliance requirements for sites involved in the outbound transportation of regulated materials, including proper shipping papers, packaging, and labeling standards. Audit Program and Inspection Readiness Architect the enterprise internal compliance audit program from the ground up -- establishing audit scope, methodology, scoring frameworks, and corrective action workflows that give the organization a consistent, repeatable mechanism for identifying and closing compliance gaps. Conduct or coordinate compliance audits across the network, producing written findings, risk ratings, and actionable corrective action plans for site and regional leaders. Manage the enterprise corrective action tracking system for compliance findings, ensuring closure within defined timelines and verifying effectiveness. Prepare the network for external regulatory inspections and customer audits -- developing site-readiness checklists, conducting pre-audit walkthroughs, and providing on-site support during inspections where required. Maintain an inspection and audit calendar for all sites, tracking regulatory visit history, findings, and corrective action status in a centralized compliance management system. Produce regular compliance performance reporting for the Head of HSS and senior leadership, including audit scores, open findings, and trend analysis. Regulatory Intelligence and Policy Development Establish and operate a systematic regulatory intelligence function -- monitoring federal and state activity across OSHA, EPA, FDA, and DOT to identify proposed rules, final rules, and enforcement trends before they affect Stord’s operations. Translate regulatory changes into policy updates, program revisions, and implementation plans; communicate impacts clearly to the Head of HSS, Regional Managers, and site teams. Own Stord’s compliance policy library: drafting, reviewing, updating, and version-controlling all compliance-related policies and written programs. Serve as subject matter authority for compliance questions from Regional Managers, Site Managers, Operations, Legal, and Customer Success. Contribute compliance expertise to new site launch processes, automation deployments, and major operational changes to ensure regulatory requirements are built in from the start. Reporting, Data & Dashboards Build the enterprise compliance reporting infrastructure from the ground up -- designing the metrics framework, data architecture, and dashboard suite that give the Head of HSS and senior leadership a real-time, accurate view of compliance performance across the network. Define the enterprise compliance KPI set selecting the leading and lagging indicators that most accurately represent program health, regulatory risk, and operational compliance posture -- and ensuring those metrics are collected consistently across all sites. Design and own compliance dashboards that surface OSHA recordable rates, audit scores, corrective action aging, training completion rates, certification status, and regulatory inspection outcomes in a format that is actionable at the executive, regional, and site levels. Build data collection standards and reporting protocols across the network -- establishing how compliance data is captured, validated, and submitted from sites and regions to ensure the enterprise view is reliable and comparable. Develop regular compliance performance reporting cadences for the Head of HSS, Operations leadership, and the Safety and Security Steering Committee -- translating raw data into clear narratives, trend analysis, and risk-flagged summaries that drive decisions. Identify systemic compliance risks and program gaps through data analysis -- surfacing patterns across sites, regions, and regulatory domains that individual site or regional reports would not reveal in isolation. Partner with Operations, Finance, and Technology to integrate compliance data into broader business reporting platforms, ensuring compliance metrics are visible alongside operational and financial performance indicators. Maintain a compliance metrics library and reporting archive that provides the organization with historical performance data, audit trails, and the documentation needed to demonstrate program maturity to regulators, customers, and insurers. Training Governance and Compliance Capability Building Build the enterprise compliance training architecture: designing the training matrix, specifying required topics, applicable employee populations, delivery methods, and completion frequencies across all regulatory domains -- the standard that governs what compliance training looks like at every Stord site. Develop compliance training content and supporting materials for use by site and regional teams -- including written programs, quick reference guides, audit checklists, and SOP templates. Govern training completion compliance across the network through record audits and gap reporting; escalate systemic deficiencies to Regional Managers with a remediation timeline. Build and maintain a compliance resource library accessible to site and regional HSS teams, enabling consistent program delivery without requiring centralized instruction. Required Qualifications Experience 7+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, EHS program management, or a related discipline in a warehouse, fulfillment, manufacturing, or logistics environment. Demonstrated expertise across multiple regulatory domains -- OSHA, EPA, and GMP/GDP -- with hands-on program ownership experience in each. Experience managing compliance programs across a multi-site network, including audit program design and regulatory agency interaction. Track record of translating complex regulatory requirements into practical, scalable operational programs. Technical Knowledge Deep working knowledge of OSHA General Industry standards, recordkeeping requirements, and enforcement processes. Strong familiarity with EPA compliance obligations applicable to warehouse and fulfillment operations, including Tier II, SPCC, and RCRA. Working knowledge of GMP and GDP standards as they apply to regulated fulfillment, distribution, and third-party logistics. Experience with DOT Hazmat regulations (49 CFR) governing the handling, storage, and transportation of regulated materials. Proficiency with compliance management systems, audit platforms, document control tools, and regulatory tracking resources. Credentials (Preferred) CSP, ASP, or equivalent safety certification preferred. CHMM (Certified Hazardous Materials Manager) or equivalent preferred. REHS, REM, or equivalent environmental compliance credential a plus. GMP/GDP auditor certification or equivalent regulated industry compliance credential preferred. OSHA 500 or OSHA 30-hour General Industry required; advanced OSHA coursework preferred. Who You Are A regulatory expert, not a generalist -- you have deep knowledge in at least two of the core compliance domains and the intellectual curiosity to go deep in the others. A program architect -- you build compliance infrastructure that scales across dozens of sites without requiring your personal presence at each one. Your programs are self-sustaining by design. Proactive and ahead of the curve -- you’re tracking rulemaking before it becomes a requirement and updating programs before an inspector identifies the gap. A credible advisor -- Regional Managers and site teams bring you their hardest compliance questions because you give clear, practical answers grounded in the actual regulation. Detail-oriented without losing the thread -- you can manage a 30-site audit calendar and still see the systemic risk patterns that individual findings represent. A strong written communicator -- your policies are readable, your audit reports are actionable, and your regulatory summaries make complex requirements understandable to operators.

jd_text: Product Manager Job Description: Thomson Reuters is seeking a dynamic Product Manager to drive the development and commercialization of innovative analytical solutions, ensuring alignment with customer needs and strategic business objectives. The Product Manager owns the vision, direction, and priorities for a larger, more complex, or strategic product or group of products, managing the full product lifecycle from strategic planning through to tactical execution. They understand the needs of the customers the product is designed to serve in depth, communicate those needs crisply across the organization, and work with design and engineering to translate them into clear priorities, compelling roadmaps, and high-impact solutions. They reason across the full system understanding how decisions in their area impact adjacent products, teams, and the end-to-end customer experience and bring the right people into the room to make trade-offs visible. They confidently shape product direction with a clear view of commercial impact, balancing short-term delivery with long-term system health and customer trust, and maintain a sharp sense of focus on the right problems, the right customers, and the right investments, treating scope creep and the impulse to build for everyone as the strategic risks they are. The balance between tactical execution and strategic vision is critical at this level, as is the ability to coordinate across multiple functions simultaneously and to lead in building AI-enabled products and experiences with depth and credibility. This is a hybrid role Key Responsibilities: Lead the entire product lifecycle from ideation through launch and post-launch optimization, focusing on analytical solutions. Conduct thorough market research and competitive analysis to identify new opportunities and inform product strategy. Translate complex customer needs and market insights into clear product requirements and user stories. Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, design, sales, and marketing teams to ensure successful product development and commercialization. Develop and execute go-to-market strategies, including pricing, positioning, and promotional activities. Monitor product performance, gather customer feedback, and iterate on features to drive continuous improvement and customer engagement. Effectively communicate product vision, roadmap, and updates to internal and external stakeholders. Manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritizing tasks to maximize organizational efficiency. Required Qualifications: Proven experience in product management, particularly with analytical solutions. Strong understanding of product development methodologies and product commercialization processes. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly. Demonstrated ability in group problem solving and strategic execution. Proficiency in computer literacy, including advanced skills in Microsoft Office Suite. Experience with marketing and customer engagement strategies. Highly organized, detail-oriented, and capable of effective multitasking. Strong researching abilities to inform product decisions and market understanding. Preferred Qualifications: Experience managing tax, accounting, or other regulated professional-services software, ideally enterprise products serving large firms. Hands-on experience building and launching AI/ML-enabled products or features, including working with engineering on responsible AI, data quality, and governance. Demonstrated ownership of commercial outcomes such as adoption, retention, and revenue, with experience in pricing, packaging, and business-case development. Experience mentoring junior Product Managers and leading cross-functional initiatives without direct authority. Familiarity with product analytics and customer-feedback tools (e.g., Pendo, Amplitude) to drive data-informed prioritization. Experience with Agile practices and road mapping/backlog tools (e.g., Azure DevOps, Lucid). They own translating those standards into consistent regional execution and are accountable for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that drive financial, operational, and asset loss across their region. The Regional Manager is accountable for: Regional safety, compliance, and loss prevention performance metrics and trend improvement. Translating enterprise standards into site-level execution — ensuring consistent, high-quality program delivery across every facility in the region. Hiring, onboarding, and developing a regional team of HSS and loss prevention professionals. Loss prevention strategy and shrink reduction for their region — including investigation oversight, security controls, and carrier/vendor accountability. Regional compliance posture across OSHA, state regulations, and Stord internal standards. Escalation management: serving as the regional decision-maker for incidents, investigations, and regulatory inquiries. Risk ownership: proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across the region that could result in financial loss, operational disruption, or damage to people and assets — before they become incidents. Key Responsibilities Team Leadership and Development Recruit, hire, and onboard site-level safety and loss prevention professionals within the region. Set clear performance expectations, conduct regular coaching conversations, and deliver structured feedback and development plans. Build a high-accountability, growth-oriented team culture within the regional HSS function. Identify talent gaps and succession needs; develop internal candidates for expanded roles. Facilitate regional team meetings, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving across sites. Safety Program Execution Deploy and sustain enterprise safety standards across all regional facilities, ensuring consistent implementation. Conduct or oversee facility safety audits, gap assessments, and corrective action tracking. Support site leaders and operations teams in embedding safety into daily standard work and leadership routines. Lead or oversee incident investigations within the region, ensuring root cause analysis quality and timely corrective action closure. Represent the region in enterprise safety forums, surfacing trends, risks, and improvement opportunities to the Head of HSS. Coordinate peak readiness reviews to ensure safety standards are maintained through volume surges and labor onboarding. Loss Prevention and Asset Protection Own regional loss prevention strategy, including shrink reduction targets, security controls, and investigative outcomes. Oversee internal investigations related to theft, fraud, and inventory discrepancy — escalating to HR, Legal, or Law Enforcement as appropriate. Analyze loss trends across the region and drive root cause resolution through operational and procedural improvements. Manage CCTV, access control, and physical security standards across regional sites, partnering with facilities teams on remediation. Build relationships with carrier partners, vendors, and law enforcement contacts to support loss prevention outcomes. Partner with Operations and Finance to quantify and report on shrink, damage, and loss impact at the regional level. Compliance and Regulatory Management Ensure all regional facilities maintain compliance with applicable OSHA, state, and local regulations. Serve as the regional point of contact for regulatory inspections, responding to inquiries and coordinating any required corrective actions. Monitor regulatory changes with regional applicability and coordinate with the Head of HSS to update procedures accordingly. Oversee Hazmat compliance within the region, including proper storage, labeling, training, and incident reporting. Support site-level readiness for customer-required certifications such as GMP, GDP, CTPAT, or TAPA where applicable within the region. Metrics, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement Own regional safety and loss prevention KPIs, delivering regular performance reporting to the Head of HSS and regional operations leadership. Drive trend analysis across regional sites to identify systemic risks before they become incidents. Manage corrective action pipelines within the region, ensuring timely closure and verified effectiveness. Champion near-miss and hazard reporting culture across sites, tracking participation rates as a leading indicator. Partner with Ops Excellence to integrate safety and loss prevention improvements into standard operating procedures. New Site Launches and Network Changes Lead HSS readiness for new site launches within the region, including safety walkthroughs, program onboarding, and staff training. Support automation and equipment commissioning activities from a safety perspective within the region. Ensure staffing and program coverage scales appropriately as the regional network grows. Multi-site experience in 3PL, eCommerce fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing environments. Demonstrated experience in loss prevention investigation, shrink management, or asset protection in a high-volume logistics or retail environment. Technical Knowledge Working knowledge of OSHA standards, state-specific safety regulations, and compliance program management. Hands-on experience managing physical security systems, including CCTV, access control, and inventory protection protocols. Familiarity with incident investigation methodologies and corrective action systems. Comfort with Hazmat regulations and controlled substance handling requirements in a warehouse or fulfillment context. Experience using safety and loss prevention data to drive operational decisions. Credentials (Preferred) ASP, CSP, or equivalent safety certification, or active pursuit of one. Wicklander-Zulawski (WZ), Reid Technique, or equivalent interviewing certification preferred. Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement background a plus. Familiarity with CTPAT, TAPA, or SOC-related security requirements a plus. Leadership Profile A builder and developer of people — energized by growing a team, not just managing one. Highly credible with frontline associates and site operations leaders; earns trust through presence and follow-through. Capable of holding the line on standards while maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with operations partners. Analytical and data-driven; able to translate metrics into clear narratives and actionable plans for regional and executive audiences. Comfortable in ambiguity — able to triage competing priorities, escalate appropriately, and keep the team focused under pressure. Strong written and verbal communicator; able to represent the region in enterprise forums and deliver clear guidance to site teams.
